title: Continue responsibility when an important consequence cannot be undone

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Irreversibility can concern an object, an opportunity or an effect of harm. Repair may still help while remaining incomplete. Continuing responsibility does not require obtaining absolution or pretending a substitute is identical.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Fictional Jo discarded Rae’s unique handwritten note without permission; it cannot be recovered. Rae permits one short written acknowledgment and declines a replacement. Jo also missed an optional final exhibition whose closing date cannot change; nobody else relied on attendance. These are different losses: a wrong to another person and a missed personal opportunity.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Compare responsibility and possible next conduct in both cases. Draft the acknowledgment within Rae’s limit and a handling rule that can actually be applied.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A person pays an agreed repair cost but an irreplaceable memory remains lost. Is restitution necessarily either worthless or complete?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Own the discarded note, accept the declined replacement and never discard others’ papers without permission. The exhibition needs acknowledgment of a missed opportunity, not an invented apology debt to a victim. Later fiction: Jo places an uncertain paper in an agreed holding tray; the lost note remains lost. Partial: prevention without owning impact. Incorrect: demand forgiveness or claim the tray restores the note.
criteria: Different irreversible losses carry different responsibilities
Partial repair is neither erased nor inflated
Future conduct does not demand absolution

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: Neither. The agreed payment can be a real partial repair while the irreparable loss remains. Do not force gratitude, restored trust or a claim that nothing further matters.
